quickstart.lead: Community scores for games, movies, TV series and books — 0 to 100, in six categories per item — over a read-only JSON API.
quickstart.keyBody: Open your API dashboard and create a key. It starts with hx_live_ and is shown only once — store it in an environment variable, never in client-side code:
quickstart.freePlan: The Free plan includes {quota} requests in total — enough to build and test an integration.
quickstart.requestBody: The base URL is {baseUrl}. Every endpoint is a GET. Here are the five best-rated games:
quickstart.hostNote: The same API also answers on the website host: {siteUrl}. Paths, parameters and responses are identical.
quickstart.responseBody: Lists return data plus a next_cursor for the next page. Field names are snake_case and dates are ISO 8601. score and categories are null until an item has 5 ratings.
quickstart.nextDetail: Fetch one item with {path} for external ids, trailers and the licensed synopsis.
quickstart.nextLookup: Map ids you already have with {path} (also steam, igdb, tmdb, isbn13, openlibrary, wikidata).
quickstart.nextGuides: Handle <errors>errors</errors> and <limits>rate limits</limits>, then browse the <reference>API reference</reference>.
quickstart.sdkBody: Typed clients are generated from the OpenAPI document: TypeScript ({tsPackage}) and Python ({pyPackage}). They are not on npm/PyPI yet — build them from sdks/ in the repository until the first release.

authentication.lead: Every request is authenticated with a secret API key sent as a Bearer token.
authentication.bearerBody: Send the key in the Authorization header. Keys look like hx_live_ followed by 32 letters and digits. Query-string keys are not accepted, so keys never end up in access logs or browser history.
authentication.unauthorized: A missing, malformed, unknown or revoked key returns 401 with {problemCode} and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header.
authentication.manageCreate: Create and revoke keys at <link>/profile/api</link> (verified email required, up to 5 active keys).
authentication.manageOnce: The full key is shown once. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored; we cannot recover it for you.
authentication.manageRevoke: Revocation is immediate. Rotate by creating a new key, deploying it, then revoking the old one.
authentication.manageShared: All keys of an account share the same plan, quota and per-second rate limit.
authentication.securityNote: Call the API from your server. A key embedded in a web page or mobile app can be extracted and used up your quota. If a key leaks, revoke it right away.

errors.lead: Errors use RFC 9457 problem details with a stable machine-readable code.
errors.formatBody: Every error has Content-Type: application/problem+json. Branch on code (stable) rather than on title or detail (human text that may change). type links to the matching section below, and request_id equals the X-Request-Id header — include it when you contact support.

bad_request.title: Invalid request
bad_request.when: A query parameter is unknown or out of range, the cursor was tampered with or belongs to another query, or limit is above your plan's page size (10 on Free). errors lists each problem with its path.
bad_request.fix: Fix the listed parameters. Not counted against your quota when the parameters fail validation.

unauthorized.title: Missing or invalid API key
unauthorized.when: No Authorization: Bearer header, a malformed key, or a key that does not exist or was revoked.
unauthorized.fix: Check the header and the key at <link>/profile/api</link>. Never retried automatically.

payment_required.title: Quota exhausted
payment_required.when: The quota is exhausted: the 100 lifetime requests on Free, or the monthly quota on paid plans. The body includes plan and limit.
payment_required.fix: Upgrade your plan at <link>/pricing</link>. Paid quotas reset on the 1st of each month (UTC).

forbidden.title: Forbidden
forbidden.when: The account that owns the key is suspended.

not_found.title: Not found
not_found.when: Unknown item id, an id that belongs to another type (e.g. a game id under /movies), an unknown type path, or no match for /lookup.
not_found.fix: Check the id and the type. Lookups require an exact id (e.g. tt0111161).

rate_limited.title: Too many requests
rate_limited.when: More requests per second than your plan allows. The Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait. Not counted against your quota.
rate_limited.fix: Wait Retry-After seconds and retry; space out bursts or upgrade for a higher rate.

internal_error.title: Internal error
internal_error.when: Something failed on our side. The request is refunded to your quota.
internal_error.fix: Retry with exponential backoff. If it persists, send us the request_id.

service_unavailable.title: Service unavailable
service_unavailable.when: A dependency is temporarily down. Comes with Retry-After.

errors.retriesBody: Retry only 429, 500 and 503, honouring Retry-After when present and backing off exponentially otherwise. Every endpoint is a read-only GET, so retries are always safe.

pagination.lead: List endpoints use opaque cursors: stable under inserts, fast at any depth.
pagination.howBody: GET /games, /movies, /series and /books return {shape}. To get the next page, repeat the same request with {param}. When next_cursor is null you reached the end.
pagination.sameParams: Keep every other parameter identical. A cursor from another sort returns 400.
pagination.opaque: Cursors are opaque: do not parse or build them, their format may change.
pagination.stable: Ordering is stable: ties are broken by item id, and unscored or undated items always come last.
pagination.limitBody: limit defaults to 10. The maximum depends on your plan: {free} on Free, {paid} on Pro and Business. A larger value returns 400 bad_request — the API never silently truncates. Each page counts as one request.
pagination.searchBody: GET /search is not paginated: it returns the best matches (up to 50) for a query, best first.

limits.lead: Each plan has a request quota, a per-second rate limit and a maximum page size.
limits.countEvery: Every authenticated request that reaches an endpoint counts as one, including 404s.
limits.countNot: Not counted: 401, 400 for invalid parameters, 429 and any 5xx (refunded).
limits.countUsage: GET /me/usage counts too — read the response headers of your regular calls when you can.
limits.countReset: Paid quotas reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of each month. The Free quota never resets.
limits.headersBody: Successful responses tell you where you stand (IETF RateLimit header fields):
limits.headerLimit: Requests in the current period (your plan quota).
limits.headerReset: Seconds until the quota resets; 0 for the lifetime Free quota.
limits.headerRetry: On 429 and 503: seconds to wait before retrying.
limits.exceedingNote: Too many requests per second → 429 rate_limited: wait Retry-After seconds. Quota exhausted → 402 payment_required: upgrade your plan; retrying will not help until the reset.

changelog.lead: The version is part of the path. v1 only changes in backwards-compatible ways.
changelog.policyAdditive: Within /v1 we only make additive changes: new endpoints, new optional parameters, new response fields, new enum values in categories keys for new types, and new error detail texts. Ignore unknown fields and do not rely on field order.
changelog.policyBreaking: Breaking changes — removing or renaming a field, changing a type, making a parameter required — ship as a new path (/v2). Error code values, category keys and sort names are part of the contract.
changelog.deprecationWindow: A deprecated version keeps working for at least 6 months after its successor is released.
changelog.deprecationHeaders: Its responses carry Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) headers with the date it stops working, plus a Link to this page.
changelog.deprecationEmail: Account owners with recent traffic on the old version are emailed at deprecation and 30 days before sunset.
changelog.timeToBeatBody: ItemDetail.time_to_beat: crowdsourced median hours and report count for main, extras and completionist on games (median_hours is null under 3 reports); null for movies, series and books.
changelog.firstLists: Lists, details and genres for games, movies, series and books.

policy.title: Privacy policy
policy.description: What personal data we collect, why, for how long, and how to exercise your rights.
policy.intro: This policy explains how {appName} handles personal data when you browse the site, create an account, rate items, contact us or use the paid API. It is written to meet the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018) and the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

body.0: The service operator is the controller for the data described here and is the encarregado. Privacy requests go to privacy@hexascore.app or the contact form (choose "Questions"). We answer within 15 days.
Account: name, email, nickname, password (stored only as a one-way hash), sign-in method (email and password, or Google), two-factor settings and the date you scheduled a deletion, if any.
body.1: Activity: your ratings (six categories, 0–100), item status, lists, follows and profile privacy choice.
body.2: Technical: IP address and browser user agent attached to active sessions, and short-lived counters used to block abuse (rate limiting and bot protection).
body.3: Contact messages: the name, email, subject and text you send us.
body.4: API and billing: API key metadata (we store only a hash of the key), request counts, plan, credits and invoices. Card payments are handled by Stripe; we never see or store full card numbers.

body.0: To provide the service you asked for — account, ratings, API access and billing (performance of a contract).
body.1: To keep the service secure, prevent fraud, spam and bots, and compute community scores (legitimate interest).
body.2: To load optional third-party video embeds, only after you allow them (consent, which you can withdraw at any time).
body.3: To keep billing records required by tax law (legal obligation).

body.0: We only use essential cookies: the session cookie that keeps you logged in, short-lived two-factor cookies, and the locale, theme and consent cookies. We use no advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
body.1: Optional analytics load only after you allow them. Trailers are served from youtube-nocookie.com and only load after you allow embeds in the cookie banner.
body.2: When you follow an affiliate link to Amazon or Mercado Livre you leave our site; those stores set their own cookies under their own policies.

body.0: We do not sell personal data. We share it only with providers that process it on our behalf: Railway (hosting, database, metrics and logs), Resend (transactional email), Stripe (payments), Google (only if you choose "Continue with Google") and Telegram (operator alerts).
body.1: Some of these providers are located outside your country, including in the United States. Transfers use the safeguards those laws allow.
body.2: Catalogue metadata from IGDB and TMDB is shown with the attribution those sources require. Community catalogue contributions stay under the A-07 licence.

body.0: Account data is kept while your account exists. When you delete your account, it enters a 30-day grace period during which you can log in and cancel. After that, your name, email, nickname, sessions, sign-in methods and two-factor data are erased and the account is anonymized.
body.1: Your ratings are kept after deletion without any link to your identity, as "Deleted user", so community scores are not distorted.
body.2: Contact messages are kept for up to 2 years; billing records for as long as tax law requires (currently 5 years in Brazil); security logs, the session IP address and the user agent for up to 30 days. Opt-in client reports are kept for 7 days. Export files are kept for 24 hours.

body.0: Under the LGPD and the GDPR you can confirm whether we process your data, access it, correct it, ask for anonymisation or deletion, receive a portable copy, know who we share it with, object to processing based on legitimate interest, and withdraw consent.
body.1: You can edit your name, password, two-factor settings and profile privacy, turn off personalised recommendations, and delete your account, in your profile. For anything else, use the contact form or privacy@hexascore.app. You may also complain to the Brazilian data protection authority (ANPD) or to your local supervisory authority.

body.0: Passwords are hashed, all traffic uses HTTPS, sessions use HttpOnly cookies, and you can protect your account with two-factor authentication. No system is perfectly secure; if we learn of an incident that affects you, we will notify you and the authorities as the law requires.
The service is not directed to children. You must be at least 13 years old — or the minimum age for digital consent in your country, if higher — to create an account.
We will update this page when our practices change and change the date above. Material changes are announced on the site or by email before they take effect.

terms.title: Terms of use and cookies
terms.description: The rules for using the site, your account, ratings, the paid API and affiliate links.
terms.intro: By using {appName} — the site or the API — you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.

body.0: We run a database of games, movies, TV series and books where registered users score each work in six categories from 0 to 100. Community scores are averages of user ratings and are shown only after an item has at least 5 ratings.
body.1: Item metadata comes from open sources and public store data: Wikidata (CC0), Wikipedia, Open Library, Steam and GOG. Synopses from Wikipedia are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 and are shown with their license and a link to the original article. Covers come from Open Library, Steam, GOG or Wikimedia Commons; when the license requires it, the item page credits the source, author and license. Links to external scores (such as IMDb or Metacritic) are provided for reference; those scores, the cover art and all trademarks belong to their owners.

body.0: Provide accurate information, keep one account per person and keep your credentials secret. We recommend enabling two-factor authentication. Nicknames must not impersonate others or be offensive.
body.1: We may suspend or close accounts that break these terms, manipulate scores or abuse the service.

body.0: You can rate each work once and edit your rating at any time. Ratings must reflect your honest opinion: using multiple accounts, bots or paid ratings to manipulate scores is forbidden.
body.1: You grant us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free and perpetual license to store your ratings and use them to compute and publish aggregated scores, including after your account is deleted, in anonymized form.

body.0: Do not scrape the website — use the public API instead. Do not attempt to bypass rate limits, bot protection or access controls, interfere with the service, or use it for anything illegal.

API keys are personal and secret; you are responsible for requests made with your keys. Each plan has a request quota, a maximum page size and a rate limit, listed on the pricing page. The free plan includes 100 requests per account in total and requires a verified email; paid plans have a monthly quota. Requests that fail because of an error on our side are not counted. Once you reach the quota or the rate limit, requests are refused until the quota renews or you add credits.
body.1: The API returns only our own data (scores and community statistics), open metadata and external identifiers. You must not use it to redistribute third-party data that we only link to. We may change or retire API versions with reasonable notice.

body.0: Paid plans are billed in advance. By card, through Stripe, plans are monthly subscriptions that renew automatically until cancelled; you can cancel or change your card in the billing portal. By PIX, through AbacatePay (Brazilian reais only), you buy 1 month or 12 months (12 months for the price of 10); PIX periods do not renew automatically and we email you 7 days and 1 day before they end. Prices, currency and taxes are shown before you pay.
body.1: Extra credits can only be bought with an active Pro or Business plan; they do not expire and are used after the monthly quota.
body.2: You can cancel at any time and keep access until the end of the paid period. Where the law grants you a right of withdrawal (for example, 7 days under art. 49 of the Brazilian Consumer Code), you can exercise it through the contact form and receive a refund as the law provides. If you are charged twice for the same period (for example, a PIX payment while a card subscription is active), we refund the duplicate payment.

body.0: Some book and game pages include links to Amazon and Mercado Livre. These are affiliate links: we may earn a commission on qualifying purchases, at no extra cost to you. Affiliate links are labeled on the page and never influence scores. Prices, availability, purchases and returns are the responsibility of each store.
We use only essential cookies (session, security and preferences) and load video embeds only with your consent. Details are in the Privacy policy.

You can delete your account in your profile. Deletion takes effect after a 30-day grace period during which you can log in and cancel it. Your ratings remain in the community scores anonymously. When the deletion takes effect, your API keys are revoked and an active card subscription is cancelled with no further charges.

The service and the API are provided "as is". We work to keep data accurate and the service available, but we do not guarantee that information is complete or error-free, or that the service will be uninterrupted. To the extent allowed by law, our liability is limited to the amount you paid us in the 12 months before the claim. Nothing in these terms limits rights that consumer law does not allow to be limited.

We may update these terms; material changes are announced in advance and continued use means acceptance. These terms are governed by the laws of Brazil, without prejudice to the mandatory consumer protections of the country where you live.
Questions about these terms, withdrawal or refund requests and privacy requests can be sent through the contact form.

deleteAccount.title: How to delete your HexaScore account
deleteAccount.intro: You can delete your account yourself, in the app or on the website. No support request is needed.

steps.0: Log in and open your profile.
steps.1: Choose "Delete my account" and confirm after the 10-second countdown.
steps.2: You are logged out on every device.

deleteAccount.grace: Deletion takes effect after 30 days. Until then you can log in and cancel it.
deleteAccount.erased: When it takes effect your name, email, nickname, picture, password, sign-in links and API keys are erased, and any card subscription is cancelled.
deleteAccount.kept: Your ratings stay in the community scores without any link to you, as "Deleted user".

score.title: How HexaScore scores work
score.intro: Every score is a weighted average of community ratings. The rules below are public and versioned.
score.categoriesIntro: Each title type is rated in six categories.
score.input: Rate each category from 0.5 to 10 stars in half-star steps. Click or tap a star half, or focus the control and use the arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home, End and Delete.
score.formula: The score is a Bayesian weighted mean: each rating counts with a weight, and a prior pulls titles with few ratings toward the type average. The result is shown as stars from 0 to 10 with one decimal.
score.minimum: A score is shown only after 5 counted ratings.
score.confidence: Confidence is low from 5 ratings, medium from 15 ratings with a small spread, and high from 50 ratings with a very small spread.
score.weights: A rating weighs more when the account is older and when the user marked the title as played, watched or read. New accounts and ratings without a status weigh less.
score.release: Titles can be rated only from their release date. Ratings sent earlier do not count until then.
score.burst: A sudden spike of ratings on one title temporarily limits new ratings from young accounts and shows a notice. Staff review the burst and either approve or exclude the affected ratings.
score.caps: Each account can add a limited number of new ratings and edits per day.
score.versions: Formula changes are announced at least 14 days before they apply. The active version is version 1.
